newsitem.title: MEXICO: INTERVIEW- CNA interested in acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW- CNA interested in acquisitions.

text.p: CNA Financial Corp would be most interested in making acquisitions in the health and personal auto and homeowners insurance sectors as part of its strategy for growth, CNA chief executive Dennis Chookaszian said.

Meanwhile, CNA, taking note of the increasing influence of the Internet, recently acquired a minority stake in Internet insurance broker InsWeb and may increase its stake over time, Chookaszian told Reuters in an interview this week at an International Insurance Society conference here.
"We are very significantly committed to the technology side of what we do," he said.
And, he said, "we're looking now at making some additional investments in technology-related enterprises," such as banking at home through personal computers.

Chookaszian also said he was optimistic about the outlook for the company's new employee leasing business, which he believes could gain scale as the indusry consolidates, giving CNA a new, large distribution channel. But Chookaszian said CNA plans to maintain its multi-line structure with operations in life, health and property-casualty insurance.
CNA currently writes about 16 billion in premiums, with about 11 billion coming from its property-casualty operations and about five billion from its life and health businesses, he said.
He said CNA would consider acquisitions in each of those areas but said some of those sectors are more attractive than others.

"The two markets that are changing the most rapidly, where we have the greatest opportunity right now, are the health insurance markets and the personal insurance -- personal auto and homeowners," he said.
"Those are the two areas where we are most interested in seeing if we can find partners and acquisition possibilities," he said.
In life insurance, he said, CNA plans to build scale by taking on back office computer processing work from other life insurers.
He said he also would consider an acquisition in this area, noting that each of CNA's businesses "has to compete like an independent company."

Although CNA does not plan to sell off any of its main businesses the way some of its competitors have in recent months, he said the company may form stand-alone subsidiaries from some of its current businesses and then spin off publicly traded minority stakes in them.
That is the plan underway for CNA's surety business.
In December, CNA agreed to merge its surety business with Capsure Holdings Corp to form a new stock company, CNA Surety Corp, which would be the largest surety company in the United States.

CNA would have about a 60 percent stake in CNA Surety and the rest would be publicly traded. Terms of the deal were modified on Tuesday and could force CNA to take a potentially smaller stake in CNA Surety.
"Over time, what we will likely do is a similar thing with several other parts of our organization -- setting up independent capital structures," Chookaszian said.
Candidates for such a structure could include CNA's reinsurance, life and personal auto and homeowners insurance businesses, he said.
"All of those could at some point be independent structures," he said, that would remain affiliated with CNA.
